daily.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
daily.summary: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.

daily.title: Iran dismisses report of alleged 'dirty bomb' attack on Washington
daily.summary: Iran has said CNN's claim that Tehran would attack Washington with a "dirty bomb" was an attempt to manufacture further legitimacy to continue the war. Trump has said his administration takes the claim "very seriously."

daily.title: APEC summit: What Trump, Xi and Putin want
daily.summary: Trump, Xi and Putin will hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of APEC. With different priorities on trade, Ukraine, Iran and arms control, what does each leader hope to gain?

daily.title: EU, ASEAN pursue deeper trade ties, but hurdles remain as businesses struggle with informal barriers
daily.summary: 2027 could be a landmark year for EU–Southeast Asia trade, with several deals nearing completion. But the harder task will be to ensure that businesses actually use them.

daily.title: Guinea jails 200 in wildcat gold mining crackdown
daily.summary: A Conakry court has jailed 22 former local officials from the gold-rich northeastern Siguiri region, as well as 200 people accused of illegal mining. It's part of a wider crackdown that sent thousands fleeing into Mali.

daily.title: US flexes climate action muscle at COP31 despite Trump no-show
daily.summary: The US government is snubbing UN climate talks in Turkey. That's prompted a delegation of American lawmakers, mayors and governors to make the trip instead, aiming to show climate action in the US is alive and well.

daily.title: Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
daily.summary: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

daily.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
daily.summary: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.

daily.title: Ukraine updates: Russia-Crimea bridge appears destroyed after strike
daily.summary: Zelenskyy said a strike on the Kerch bridge in Crimea was in response to continued Russian attacks targeting his country's infrastructure. Meanwhile, two bridges were hit in Russian attacks on Kyiv. DW has more.

daily.title: Could the Airbus' €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
daily.summary: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.

daily.title: Turkish authorities raid opposition Sozcu news channel, appoint new management
daily.summary: Turkish authorities have raided the Istanbul offices of Sozcu TV, halting broadcasts, appointing a trustee and opening an investigation. This marks another crackdown on pro-opposition television channels in Turkey.

daily.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
daily.summary: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.

daily.title: What makes 'Grand Theft Auto VI' more than just a game?
daily.summary: When "GTA VI" is released on November 19, millions of people worldwide will rush to their consoles to play it. How has this video game created such a cross-generational buzz?

daily.title: Trump kicks off Asia tour ahead of major talks with Putin, Xi in China
daily.summary: US President Donald Trump flew into Manila for a Quad meeting before he takes off to China for a much anticipated meet with Russian and Chinese counterparts. Follow live.

daily.title: Canada, China agree to ease tariffs amid trade rows with US
daily.summary: The Canadian and Chinese leaders have vowed closer cooperation as both nations seek to reduce reliance on the US. Canada's government said it had agreed to further reduce tariffs on a range of products.

daily.title: India news: Modi proposes e-visas for ASEAN tourists
daily.summary: Speaking at the ASEAN summit in Manila, Modi said that India's development and ASEAN's prosperity are "deeply interconnected."

daily.title: Mongolian President Khurelsukh to resign amid corruption allegations
daily.summary: Khurelsukh has said he will step down over accusations that he profited from a government railway project, but said he had been "falsely accused."

daily.title: Japan scrambles jets to counter suspected Russian aircraft
daily.summary: Japan said it lodged a "very stern protest" with Moscow after two suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace.

daily.title: Germany beat Netherlands 5-0 to win Nations League group
daily.summary: Florian Wirtz scored twice as Germany cruised to a comfortable 5-0 win over the Netherlands to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday.

daily.title: United Airlines resolves tech outage that delayed flights
daily.summary: United Airlines said a system outage that delayed departures has been resolved. The disruption came on the heels of a stoppage that halted all flights to and across the US for five hours last week.

daily.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
daily.summary: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.

daily.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
daily.summary: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.

daily.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
daily.summary: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.

daily.title: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?
daily.summary: The Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has become a focal point for the far right. Many of its members and staff have ties to ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations.

weekly.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
weekly.summary: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

weekly.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
weekly.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz, Söder aim to revisit electricity tax cut
weekly.summary: The Christian Democrats are in Munich, pushing to revive some tax relief that didn't make it into the budget after talks last week. And Manuela Schwesig faces a vote on a new term as regional leader. Follow DW.

weekly.title: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?
weekly.summary: In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?

weekly.title: AI in German classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'
weekly.summary: The research points in one direction: If students aren't careful about how they use AI-enabled tools, then academic performance can plummet. It's a huge challenge for teachers.

weekly.title: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?
weekly.summary: The German economy is growing again, albeit slightly. However, economists warn that without reforms, higher productivity and solid public finances, a loss of prosperity and growing debt threaten future generations.

weekly.title: Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
weekly.summary: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

weekly.title: Germany news: Germany holds national day of remembrance
weekly.summary: Events were held for "Volkstrauertag," a day commemorating victims of war and oppression. Meanwhile, experts said the country is headed for a budget crisis.

weekly.title: How AI is likely to change Germany's job market
weekly.summary: The scale of the economic disruption caused by AI has led even conservative politicians to talk about universal basic income. But economists aren't convinced, and campaigners think we need to ask deeper questions.

weekly.title: Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt
weekly.summary: The 2027 federal budget proposal has finally been hammered out and is set for a vote in parliament. What are the government's policy priorities in defense, infrastructure, the economy and social spending?

weekly.title: Werner Holzer Prize awarded to Katja Gloger and DW's Jaafar Abdul Karim
weekly.summary: DW journalist Jaafar Abdul Karim and Russia correspondent Katja Gloger have been awarded the prestigious Werner Holzer Prize for international journalism.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
weekly.summary: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

weekly.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
weekly.summary: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, addressed via his songs and sharp wit. At 90, he's as feisty as ever.

weekly.title: Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
weekly.summary: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

weekly.title: Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
weekly.summary: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

weekly.title: The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
weekly.summary: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

weekly.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
weekly.summary: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

weekly.title: Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany
weekly.summary: Two weeks after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.

weekly.title: Germany gives sweeping powers to police, intelligence services
weekly.summary: Drone sightings and cyberattacks have heightened security concerns. How are the police preparing to meet these challenges? And how do intelligence services plan to counter threats from both domestic and foreign sources?

weekly.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
weekly.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms has cast doubt on Anthropic's looming IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

weekly.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
weekly.summary: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has said midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

weekly.title: Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget
weekly.summary: The budget committee in the Bundestag worked into the night to sign off on next year's spending plans. These include levels of new debt only eclipsed once, at the height of the COVID pandemic. DW has more.

weekly.title: Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
weekly.summary: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.

weekly.title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
weekly.summary: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.

weekly.title: Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir
weekly.summary: Written and smuggled out of prison, the 2023 Nobel Prize laureate's memoir reveals the cost of defying Iran's regime and fighting for freedom.

weekly.title: EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
weekly.summary: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

weekly.title: Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
weekly.summary: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

weekly.title: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
weekly.summary: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

weekly.title: Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
weekly.summary: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

weekly.title: UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
weekly.summary: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

weekly.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
weekly.summary: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.

weekly.title: What are fossil fuels?
weekly.summary: They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?

weekly.title: Germany news: Police raid chapters of Gremium MC biker gang
weekly.summary: Police in southwestern Germany launched major early-morning operations against a biker gang. The state of Baden-Württemberg is outlawing three of its chapters. Meanwhile, unions are planning more strikes.

weekly.title: Bundeswehr study exposes widespread sexual harassment in German military
weekly.summary: Sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known, with younger women disproportionately affected. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has called for a policy of "zero tolerance."

weekly.title: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds
weekly.summary: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.

weekly.title: Fears of rising antisemitism in Europe
weekly.summary: Holocaust survivor Regina Sluszny commemorates the victims of Auschwitz as Jewish communities across Europe face growing hostility. What does the promise of "Never Again" mean for Jewish life in Europe today?

weekly.title: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge
weekly.summary: The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant background is improving, violent youth remain a problem.

weekly.title: Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship
weekly.summary: The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.

weekly.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
weekly.summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

weekly.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
weekly.summary: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

weekly.title: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?
weekly.summary: World leaders warn that geopolitical divisions are distracting from the climate crisis as negotiations focus on clean energy and financing, while Iran calls for compensation for war-related environmental damage.

weekly.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
weekly.summary: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

weekly.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
weekly.summary: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

weekly.title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
weekly.summary: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

weekly.title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
weekly.summary: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

weekly.title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
weekly.summary: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

weekly.title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
weekly.summary: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

weekly.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
weekly.summary: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.
